extracted.intended_audience: IP office statisticians, policymakers, researchers and analysts of intellectual property statistics
extracted.subtask_description: WIPO statistical tables and explanatory notes for industrial design and plant variety data (counts, procedural metrics, definitions and data-quality caveats) used to compare office performance and filing/origin patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution on cross-office comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO collects data from IP offices using a common questionnaire and methodology. However, due to differences in industrial design procedures between offices, data cannot be fully harmonized. Therefore caution should be exercised when making comparisons across offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated in notes: procedural differences and varying reporting practices mean figures are not perfectly comparable across offices; treat cross-office comparisons with caution and consult footnotes/metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average pendency times (filing to first office action; filing to final decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average pendency times from filing date to first office action and to final decision at selected offices, 2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented per office (days). Pendency metrics are sensitive to office procedures and must be interpreted alongside procedural differences and data completeness notes (see caution on cross-office comparisons).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of examiners (FTE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of industrial design examiners for selected offices, 2019 (FTE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTE = full time equivalent. Used as a capacity metric alongside application volumes and pendency to assess office resourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application processing outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of applications processed broken down by Registered, Rejected, Withdrawn or abandoned, and Applications pending (also total applications processed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These outcome categories are used in office procedural tables (C41) to summarise processing results. The total processed may be incomplete if offices omit elements; interpret with accompanying caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent count methodology (regional offices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Equivalent counts take multiple members of the regional office into account. For equivalent count, a single application filed at a regional office is equivalent to multiple applications: each application is multiplied by the corresponding number of member states for the regional office concerned (CPVO/OAPI example).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: For CPVO applications, if the applicant resided in one of the 28 EU member states the application was counted as one resident filing and 27 filings abroad; if the applicant did not reside in an EU member state, the application was counted as 28 filings abroad. Same methodology applied to OAPI. Use equivalent counts when assessing origin activity that involves regional offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of origin (applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Origin is defined as the country of the stated address of residence of the first named applicant in an international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compile origin-based application statistics. Note that origin reporting is incomplete for some offices (see data completeness). For EU applicants filing at CPVO, filing at CPVO is treated as a resident filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of origin (registrations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Origin is defined as the country/territory of the stated residence of the holder in an international registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous to application origin but applied to holders in registrations; used in registration tables and equivalent-count calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident vs non-resident filing distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications received by offices are reported as resident (filed by applicants domiciled at the office) or non-resident (filed by applicants domiciled abroad).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several analyses and charts (e.g., contribution of resident and non-resident applications to total growth) rely on this distinction. For regional offices, special rules apply when mapping resident/non-resident to member states (see equivalent count methodology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data completeness and footnote caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Design count by origin data are incomplete, because some offices do not report the origin of applications. (b) Only Hague designation data are available and/or the office has not reported the origin of applications therefore design count by office and origin data may be incomplete. (.. indicates not available; n.a. indicates not applicable.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple footnotes identify where data are missing or only partially available. Analysts must account for incomplete origin reporting, Hague-only data, and other footnoted limitations when using tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hague international application and designation counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Designs contained in Hague international applications and designs contained in designations in Hague international applications (counts by origin and by designated Hague members).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps and top-20 lists show origins and designated members. Note: applicants residing in a non-member country can file international registrations if they have a real and effective industrial or commercial establishment within the jurisdiction of a Hague member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration design count and registrations in force
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration design count by office and by origin, equivalent registration design count by origin, Hague international registration design count, and 'In force by office' totals (2019).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess the stock of active registrations as well as new registrations; interpret alongside origin/reporting caveats and 'in force' definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total (year) estimates and grouping by income/region
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary totals for 2019 estimates and breakdowns of applications/titles by income group (high, upper middle, lower middle, low) and by region (Asia, Europe, North America, LAC, Africa, Oceania).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to analyse geographic and income-group trends (e.g., shares of filings). Changes over time reflect filing growth and may be affected by procedural or reporting changes at major offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant variety specific metrics (applications, titles issued, titles in force)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant variety metrics include trend in applications worldwide, titles issued worldwide, applications and titles by office and by origin, equivalent application counts, and titles in force (2019).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes species-agnostic counts and equivalent-count adjustments for regional offices (CPVO/OAPI). Guidance notes highlight that growth in titles may reflect processing capacity and procedural delays as well as filing behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes on processing-capacity interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: The grant or registration process takes time, so fluctuations in the volumes of plant variety titles granted may reflect changes in processing capacities or procedural delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting year-on-year changes in titles granted or pendency, consider changes in office processing capacity and backlog, not only applicant behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table-level reporting caveat: total processed may be incomplete
rubrics_metrics.description: The total number of applications processed for a given office may be incomplete due to the omission of one or several elements by the office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should not assume table totals are exhaustive; consult office footnotes and metadata before aggregating or comparing totals.
